Confirmed on v2.0.5 source, and one part of the report is narrower than stated: the v2 `curl` updater does not use GitHub Releases at all, so the missing `v2.0.7` release only breaks the *legacy* `opencode.ai/install` script (dev branch), not `/update`.

What I ran against the v2.0.5 checkout (`packages/cli/src/services/updater.ts`, `updater-action.ts` executed as-is, types stripped):

```
$ node repro.mjs
{ execPath: '/usr/bin/opencode', isCurl: false, manifest: '/usr/package.json', manifestExists: false, method: undefined }
{ current: '2.0.5', latest: '2.0.7', notify: 'notify', disable: 'none' }
{ current: '2.0.8', latest: '2.0.7', notify: 'notify' }      # no semver-gt guard, as you said
200 https://registry.npmjs.org/@opencode/cli-linux-x64/-/cli-linux-x64-2.0.7.tgz
404 https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases/download/v2.0.7/opencode-linux-x64.tar.gz
```

So the actual sequence for a pacman install:

1. `inspect()` -> `action("2.0.5","2.0.7","notify")` returns `notify` and the home screen shows the banner. `method()` is never consulted at this point.
2. Pressing Update calls `apply()` -> `install()` -> `method()`. `method()` checks only `~/.opencode/bin/opencode` and a `package.json` two levels above `process.execPath`. For `/usr/bin/opencode` that is `/usr/package.json`, which does not exist, so `installedPackage` is `undefined` and `method()` returns `undefined` -> "Installation method not found".
3. Had `method()` returned `curl`, `upgrade()` fetches `https://opencode.ai/v2/install`, and that script resolves `@opencode/cli-linux-x64@2.0.7` from registry.npmjs.org (200 above). The GitHub Releases dependency lives only in `https://opencode.ai/install`, which 307s to `raw.githubusercontent.com/.../refs/heads/dev/install` and does `releases/download/v${version}/...` (line 194 of that script). That is the 1.x installer; it cannot install 2.x from GitHub because nothing publishes assets there.

Workaround until this is fixed: the banner is driven by `run()`, which honours the policy file, so either

```
echo '{"update":"disable"}' > ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json   # or "autoupdate": false
# or
export OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE=1
```

`readPolicy()` only reads `config.json` / `opencode.json` / `opencode.jsonc` under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode` (or `$OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`), not a project-level config. A manual `/update` still goes through `check()`, which ignores the policy, but it no longer nags.

Suggested fix in `updater.ts`: have `run()` call `method()` before returning `{type:"available"}` under `notify`/`auto`, and return `undefined` (with the existing "installation method not found" log) when it is undetected. That drops the banner for distro packages without touching the manual `/update` path. Detecting the package manager itself (`pacman -Qo "$(realpath "$0")"`, `dpkg -S`, `brew --prefix`) would be a separate, nice-to-have step so the dialog can say "update via your package manager".

I'd like to work on this.

The root cause still reproduces on the current `v2` head (`3355c93efd`). v2 has a plugin readiness barrier, and its own comment names this exact case (`packages/core/src/plugin/service.ts`):

> Session entry points wait here before reading plugin-provided state such as commands, skills, hooks, and the model catalog. A cold Location activates its plugins asynchronously, so without the wait an early request observes an empty registry and admits or fails work the plugins would have shaped.

`Plugin.awaitActivation` is awaited by the session and entry-point readers — `session/command.ts:21`, `session/generate.ts:29`, `session/prompt.ts:38`, `session/runner/llm.ts:66`, `session/shell.ts:12`, `session/skill.ts:12`, `filesystem/location-watcher.ts:91`, `server/handlers/integration.ts:33`, `server/handlers/rpc.ts:11` — but not by the public read handlers this issue is about:

- `packages/server/src/handlers/provider.ts` — `provider.list` / `provider.get` read `Provider.Service` directly
- `packages/server/src/handlers/model.ts` — `model.list` reads `models.available()` directly
- `packages/server/src/handlers/agent.ts` and `packages/server/src/handlers/command.ts` — same pattern

So a cold Location can still answer these endpoints with `200 OK` and a snapshot that plugin activation has not shaped yet, which is the failure described here.

I also read the earlier attempt at this work (#36131, closed by its author after review silence, not rejected on technical grounds). It took the right direction — waiting on the existing readiness barrier before returning a successful snapshot. I'd like to redo it in that same narrow shape, reusing `Plugin.awaitActivation` and the existing timeout behaviour rather than adding a new mechanism.

If this direction is still wanted, I'll open a narrow PR that mirrors the existing pattern.

Independently tested this on current `dev` (Sep 18, `b02acc1`) on darwin-arm64 with a real
config — I want this bump to land, but there's one blocker to sort out first.

## Blocker: compiled release binaries crash under Bun 1.4.x with `splitting: true`

`build.ts` uses `minify: true, splitting: true` with `Bun.build({ compile })`. Under both
Bun 1.4.1 and 1.4.2 the resulting binary crashes on the **first agent turn**:

```
TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'node.name')
    at resolve (packages/core/src/effect/layer-node.ts:241:45)
    at recur (layer-node.ts:185:28)
    ...
    at SystemPrompt.environment (src/session/prompt.ts:1259)
```

A node in the Effect layer graph comes through as `undefined` — consistent with
cross-chunk module-init ordering under ESM splitting in compiled bundles. Not reproducible
running from source on the same Bun versions, and the 1.3.14-compiled release binary works.

With `splitting: false` the compiled binary works completely. Since CI only exercises
source mode, this would ship broken release binaries if merged unchanged. Also worth
knowing: `--version`/`serve` smoke tests don't reach this path (health/config/agent routes
return 200 on a broken binary) — my first "working" build was a false positive too.

Tracked upstream in oven-sh/bun#42837 (previously thought Android/fork-specific; stock
opencode on darwin-arm64 confirms it's general — I've added a follow-up comment there
with the full matrix and sourcemapped trace).

## Supporting data for the bump itself (with `splitting: false`)

12 sequential LLM prompts against one long-lived `opencode serve` (HTTP API, isolated data
dir, same config/auth, RSS sampled every 5 s):

| Embedded Bun | Startup RSS | After workload | Growth |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1.3.14 (v1.18.31 release binary) | 356 MB | 1138 MB | +781 MB |
| 1.4.2 (dev + this pin) | 388 MB | 751 MB | +362 MB |

Roughly half the memory growth on an identical workload. Caveats: short workload, macOS
only, no MCP/plugin churn, doesn't cover peak memory or multi-hour sessions.

If useful I can push the `splitting: false` change to a branch for you to fold in, or
leave it with the maintainers — happy either way.

Root cause in `argPath` (`packages/opencode/src/tool/shell.ts`): the bash branch only does `unquote()` on raw args, which is a no-op for unquoted words with backslash-escaped chars (`/tmp/my\ project/x` keeps the `\`). So `resolvePath` gets the literal string, `containsPath` misses, and the path looks "external" — triggering the `external_directory` prompt and, under a `"*": deny` agent rule, hard-denying the command. Fix: add a `\\X`→`X` unescape pass after `unquote()` so escaped chars collapse before `path.resolve`. PR today.

If the sessions still exist but the UI won't show them, oos can surface them: it reads `opencode.db` (SQLite) directly instead of going through the session list, so anything in the database is browsable and searchable regardless of what the UI displays. Type a keyword, Enter resumes via `opencode -s <id>`.

![oos demo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wsaaaqqq/oos/master/demo.gif)

https://github.com/wsaaaqqq/oos (MIT, single binary incl. Windows, zero config, read-only DB access)

Worth a try before downgrading — if oos lists them, your data is fine and it's purely a display/filtering problem.

The "fast access matters more than the exact UI" framing resonates — that's the bet behind oos: a keyboard-driven session switcher with no large UI surface at all. It preloads all sessions from SQLite and filters in memory on every keystroke (<1ms), so switching is type → Up/Down → Enter, across all projects at once.

![oos demo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wsaaaqqq/oos/master/demo.gif)

https://github.com/wsaaaqqq/oos (MIT, single binary, zero config)

No pinned shortcuts (Ctrl-1/2/3 is an interesting idea though) — but for the "jump back to a session in under 2 seconds" goal, a fuzzy picker over everything beats browsing per-project lists.

Reproducing on V2 — the symptom has changed since the V1 reports, so adding current data.

**Version:** `opencode v2.0.7`, macOS 26.6.2, TUI (tmux, 200x50)
**Setup:** clean scratch dir with one project command, `.opencode/commands/demo.md`

| Input | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `/demo` (slash at offset 0) | picker opens, `/demo` listed |
| `say /demo now` (`/` mid-line) | picker **opens** but shows `No matching commands` |
| `first line` ⏎ `/demo` (`/` at the start of a second line) | picker opens, `No matching commands` |
| `review this @mem` (`@` mid-line) | mention picker works, skills listed |

So on V2 it is no longer "the popover never opens" (as in #16262 / #16826): the popover opens anywhere, but the command list is only contributed to the completion options when the trigger token index is 0. Any `/` elsewhere opens an empty picker. A second line does not help either — not even line-start is enough.

`@` mentions carry no such restriction, which is the parity #16262 asked for. In a multi-line prompt the same limitation shows up for `/skills`-style invocation, so it affects skills as well as config commands.

Happy to probe a build if someone wants the mid-line and multi-line cases tested.

I hit the same issue and dug into the numbers — I believe I found the actual root cause, and it's not a timing/cycle mismatch (as speculated in #39430), but how the "Total" % is calculated.

The dashboard appears to compute Total as a **simple sum of each model's individual usage percentage** (each model's own $ used ÷ its own $ quota), rather than a dollar-weighted aggregate (total $ used across all models ÷ total $ quota across all models).

Example from my own weekly usage table:

| Model | Usage | Quota | % |
|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek V4 Pro | $3.37 | $7.50 | 44.9% |
| GLM 5.3 | $2.65 | $7.50 | 35.3% |
| GLM 5.2 | $4.72 | $30.00 | 15.7% |
| **Displayed Total** | | | **95.9%** (= 44.9 + 35.3 + 15.7) |

But my actual dollar usage was $10.74 out of a $45.00 combined quota — about **23.9%**, not 95.9%.

Three rules from that ledger, offered for whoever implements the core fix:

1. **Meter at the call boundary, not the session boundary.** Every LLM call writes an append-only cost event at the moment it happens — including the hidden ones (summaries, title generation). Anything reconstructed after the fact from session state will miss the calls that never appear in the message flow.
2. **Store `own_cost`, treat `total_cost` as a cached rollup.** Parent-chain rollups that are written once become wrong the moment a child session continues running — which is the drift you observed in `session.cost` between reads. Your "rollup ages better than a snapshot" is the right call; recomputing from events at read/audit time is what makes it stay right.
3. **Reconciliation is events ⊕ cached rollups, and drift is signal.** A periodic pass recomputing the subtree cost from the event log and comparing it against what the store reports catches silent accounting drift (the #7387 "costs decreasing" class) at audit time instead of user-report time. The core pass is a few lines (both sides cover the same cost universe — the subtree of S — so consistency shows up as OK, not false positives):

```
events  = sum(e.tokens * e.price for e in cost_events if e.session in subtree(S))
rollup  = session_store.get(S).total_cost      # what the UI currently shows
if abs(events - rollup) > epsilon:             # drift = investigate, don't auto-correct
    flag(S, events, rollup)
```
